Application Materials.content:
Your application will not be progressed if the information and evidence listed is not provided. **With your online application you will need to provide:**
1. A copy of your degree certificate and transcripts. If your degree certificate or result is pending, please upload any interim transcripts or provisional certificates.
2. A copy of your IELTS certificate, or evidence of an accepted equivalent. Please include the date of your expected test if this qualification is pending. If you have alternative acceptable evidence, such as an undergraduate degree studied in the UK, please supply this in place of an IELTS.

Interview Requirements.content: Your academic school may contact you directly if they require any further information or wish to invite you for an interview. You will receive an email asking you to check your applicant portal for more details.

Application Deadlines.content:
Start date: **28 September 2026**.
**Application Deadline:** We allocate places on a first-come, first-served basis, so we recommend you apply as early as possible. Applications normally close at the **end of August** but may close sooner if all places are filled.

Academic Requirements.content:
- You must have achieved **a 2:2 honours degree in a relevant subject area such as engineering, mathematics, or science**, or an equivalent international degree.
- For applicants from China: you will be required to have **a relevant four-year bachelor's degree from a recognised institution, with grades of approximately 80% or above** to qualify for postgraduate taught courses.

English Proficiency Requirements.content:
With your online application you will need to provide **a copy of your IELTS certificate with an overall score of 6.5 with 5.5 in all subskills**, or evidence of an accepted equivalent. Please include the date of your expected test if this qualification is pending. If you have alternative acceptable evidence, such as an undergraduate degree studied in the UK, please supply this in place of an IELTS.
Find out more about [English language requirements](https://www.cardiff.ac.uk/study/international/english-language-requirements/postgraduate). Applicants who require a Student visa to study in the UK must present an [acceptable English language qualification](https://www.cardiff.ac.uk/study/international/english-language-requirements/postgraduate) in order to meet UKVI (UK Visas and Immigration) requirements.

Program Overview.content:
Data Science and Analytics (MSc) is offered full time over 1 year with a September start. The course equips students with a theoretical understanding and practical experience of applying methods drawn from data science and analytics. Students develop in-demand skills for extracting and handling ‘big data’ and applying modelling tools to help businesses and government organisations make better decisions. On completion, graduates are well placed to progress into roles in data-intensive industries or a related research career.
The degree falls under the umbrella of the [Data Science Academy](https://www.cardiff.ac.uk/data-science-academy) (DSA), run by the School of Computer Science and Informatics in partnership with the School of Mathematics. Students benefit from the shared knowledge and skills of both Schools, although the degree is run by the School of Mathematics. Teaching takes place in the newly-built flagship building Abacws.
The programme is a two-stage programme taught over one year for a total of 180 credits: a 120-credit taught stage followed by a 60-credit research project. Students undertake 100 credits of compulsory 20-credit modules and choose a further 20 credits from optional modules. The 60-credit summer project will typically involve working with a company on a problem of real importance.
Teaching uses a mixture of lectures, seminars, computer workshops and tutorials. Programming skills and relevant software packages are taught in dedicated computer suites. Industry experts are often invited to give presentations. For the dissertation project, students are usually allocated three supervisors: two academic staff members with an interest or specialism in the research field and a sponsor supervisor from the organisation they work with during the project.
Graduates have gone on to work with companies and Government organisations including the Office for National Statistics, Lloyds Banking Group, Nationwide, British Airways, Network Rail, UK Government, The Financial Times, Virgin Media, Welsh Water and Admiral Insurance.
An important feature of the MSc programme is the project dissertation, which allows students to apply the methods and skills acquired in the taught programme to either a real-world problem or a more theoretical problem. This may involve working with an external company or organisation; in previous years students have worked with Admiral Insurance, Lloyds Banking Group, the Office for National Statistics and the National Health Service.

Curriculum.content:
Data Science and Analytics (MSc) is offered as **Full time** with **Duration: 1 year** for the September start. Other course options include Full time (17 months - January start) and Part time (3 years).
This is a two-stage programme taught over one year for a total of **180 credits**. The taught stage is **120 credits**, followed by a **60-credit research project**. You will undertake all 20-credit compulsory modules (**100 credits in total**) and choose a further **20 credits** from a list of carefully selected optional modules. The **60-credit project** undertaken in the summer will typically involve working with a company on a problem of real importance.
Core modules for year one:
| Module title | Module code | Credits |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Applied Machine Learning | CMT307 | 20 credits |
| Computational Data Science | CMT309 | 20 credits |
| Foundations of Operational Research and Analytics | MAT021 | 20 credits |
| Foundations of Statistics and Data Science | MAT022 | 20 credits |
| Dissertation | MAT099 | 60 credits |
Optional modules for year one:
| Module title | Module code | Credits |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Distributed and Cloud Computing | CMT202 | 20 credits |
| Human Centric Computing | CMT206 | 20 credits |
| Data Visualisation | CMT218 | 20 credits |
| Databases and Modelling | CMT220 | 20 credits |
| Statistics and Operational Research in Government | MAT007 | 10 credits |
| Healthcare Modelling | MAT009 | 10 credits |
| Stochastic Search and Optimisation | MAT061 | 20 credits |
| Time Series | MAT508 | 10 credits |
| Statistical Programming with R and Shiny | MAT514 | 10 credits |
The modules shown are an example of the typical curriculum. Final modules will be published one month ahead of your programme starting.
Teaching uses a mixture of lectures, seminars, computer workshops and tutorials. Programming skills and the use of relevant software packages will be taught in dedicated computer suites. For the dissertation project, three supervisors are allocated: usually two members of academic staff with an interest or specialism in the field of research and a sponsor supervisor from the organisation you will work with during your project.
Assessments may take the form of written exam papers, in-module assignments, and the project dissertation. Group work, oral presentations and poster displays may also be used.
An important feature of the MSc programme is the project dissertation. This allows you to apply the methods and skills acquired in the taught programme to either a real-world problem or a more theoretical problem. This might involve working with an external company or organisation.

Financial Aid.content:
Cardiff University's Vice-Chancellor's Postgraduate International Scholarships offer funding awards to international students across a variety of postgraduate taught programmes. Awards between **£4,000 to £10,000** will be granted to eligible postgraduate-taught students and will be offered as a tuition fee discount.
International applicants from eligible countries/territories who accept an offer for selected postgraduate programmes and pay any required deposit by the date specified on their offer letter will automatically be considered for the Vice-Chancellor's International Scholarship. This scholarship is available for students joining Cardiff University in **September 2026**.
- The standard award is **£4,000**.
- Applicants domiciled in Egypt, Kazakhstan, Kenya, Mexico, Pakistan, South Korea, Taiwan, USA, or Vietnam are eligible for **£6,000** awards.
- Applicants domiciled in Bangladesh or Nigeria are eligible for **£10,000** awards.
- Eligible applicants initially awarded unconditional offers will automatically be granted the scholarship.
- Applicants must submit their application to the University **by 31 July 2026**, hold an offer for an eligible postgraduate taught course, accept the offer and pay any applicable deposit **by 31 July 2026**, and meet all offer conditions, including English Language conditions, **by 20 August 2026**.
- Scholarship eligibility is separate from admission eligibility; applicants must achieve the published minimum academic entry requirements for their chosen programme exactly as stated on the [course pages](https://www.cardiff.ac.uk/study/postgraduate/taught/courses). Full [terms and conditions for September 2026](https://www.cardiff.ac.uk/documents/3010744-vice-chancellors-international-scholarship-terms-and-conditions-for-september-2026-entry) apply.

Deferral Admission Policy.content:
Applicants may be allowed deferred entry to a programme, subject to meeting the entry requirements and places being available. The maximum period of deferral granted will be **no more than 12 months**. Applicants wishing to defer admission for a longer period will be required to reapply. In exceptional circumstances, where an applicant may wish to seek an extension to the deferral period, the School must submit a case for approval to the Pro Vice-Chancellor (Student Experience and Academic Standards). Applicants should use the [online form](https://www.cardiff.ac.uk/study/ask-a-question) to request a deferral.
For postgraduate taught programmes, Cardiff University reserves the right to close programmes and/or to offer a deferred entry place where a programme has reached capacity, and may operate a waiting list as appropriate. The University also reserves the right to offer deferred entry to applicants who apply within 12 weeks of the start date of a programme if there is not sufficient time to process all the requirements for an applicant to start their programme by the last date of enrolment.

Conditional Admission Policy.content:
If you have not yet met the entry requirements, you can usually still apply for a course. You may receive an offer of a place on the condition that you meet the requirements before you start the course.
A **Conditional offer** means you have been offered a place, but something is missing from your application - most likely one of your supporting documents or you are still to complete one of the qualifications required to gain admission to the university. Your offer letter will clearly state what evidence needs to be supplied. Once Cardiff University has everything, your offer will change to Unconditional.
Your offer is subject to you accepting your place and meeting the exact conditions of your offer **a minimum of 14 days before the start date of your programme**, unless otherwise agreed by the university.
